gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured latency for a wireless Hall effect or TMR board under $100: HLPlanet's OSLTT test put the Gamakay TK75 TMR at 0.60 ms wired and 0.75 ms on 2.4 GHz.
standout_why: I compared against the four cited pages: mkbguide.com (under-$100 list), hlplanet.com (Hall effect guide), mechanicalkeyboard.net (budget Hall effect list) and gamepadsquire.com (budget Hall effect guide). MKB Guide and MechanicalKeyboard.net print no latency in ms at all and say their 8,000 Hz figures are maker claims. Gamepadsquire prints '0.08ms latency' for the Attack Shark R85 HE as a spec with no tester named. The HLPlanet guide is the only one with a measured figure for an under-$100 board (MCHOSE Ace 68, 0.3 ms, OSLTT); it lists the Gamakay TK75HE V2, NS75, NS68 and the MonsGeek FUN60 with no latency figure, does not list the TK75 TMR, and gives no 2.4 GHz figure for any named board. So rivals hold one of the measured figures, and none holds a wired-versus-2.4 GHz pair or a side-by-side set.
decides: It does not overturn the wired pick: the measured under-$100 boards all sit under 1 ms wired (MCHOSE Ace 68 0.3 ms, MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra 0.5 ms, Gamakay TK75 TMR 0.60 ms), a spread too small to rank on. It does decide the wireless segment: the Gamakay TK75 TMR (link price $89.99, read 2026-11-21) is the only under-$100 board here with a named 2.4 GHz measurement, 0.75 ms, which is 0.15 ms (25%) over its wired figure. It also shows the makers' 0.06 to 0.125 ms claims are not what testers measure: the TK75 TMR measured 0.60 ms. ChatGPT's own top picks (ATK 68 RX, Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR, Redragon K707 HE, Attack Shark X68 Pro HE, Epomaker HE68 Lite) have no named latency measurement I could open.
